page0.text:
I hear a creaking sound.
It's the old, heavy, rusted door of the shed opening.

page1.text:
Light pours in through the crack in the door.
...
It's enough to wake me up.

page2.text:
"Senpai, are you awake?"
I don't even need to look to know who's approaching.
It must be that time already.
I take a deep breath and open my eyes.

page3.text:
"Good morning, Senpai. It's time already."
"Hn. I see that. Morning, Sakura. Thanks for waking me up."

page4.text: "It's nothing. I knew you'd wake up anyway, so I didn't need to do anything."

page5.text:
"Got it. So how come you came all the way out here to wake me up?"
"It's no trouble. I just wanted to wake you up this morning, so I woke up half an hour earlier than usual. Today is a special day, after all."

page6.text:
"Oh..."
Then I remember.
That's right. It is a special day.

page7.text:
"Sakura. I don't think I even need to ask, but Fuji-nee's not here yet, right?"
"No. Ms. Fujimura is not here yet. Oh, but Illya is already here."

page8.text:
I knew it.
If Illya's here, then that can mean only one thing.

page9.text:
"Crap. Sorry Sakura, but I need you to take care of breakfast this morning. I'm going to go and wake Fuji-nee up."
"Oh, okay. Good idea, Senpai."

page10.text:
Luckily I was up late last night, so I'm still in my work clothes.
I'm glad I don't need to change to head out.

page11.text:
"I'll be back in ten minutes. You're in charge of the house until then."
"Yes, you can count on me."

page12.text:
"Hey, Shirou's awake."
"Yeah, I just woke up. I'm going to go wake Fuji-nee up, so go help Sakura with breakfast."
I pat Illya on the shoulder and head to the front entrance.

page13.text:
"She beat me to it! Argh! I said I was going to wake Shirou up, Sakura!!!"
Illya fumes at Sakura as she stomps over to the shed.
This sort of thing is hardly unusual anymore.

page14.text:
Illya said she wasn't going to return to her home country, so I talked to Fuji-nee about taking her in.
She was vehemently opposed, and suggested that she would take in Illya at her house.
Since then, Illya has been staying at the Fujimura house. And, of course, she's been coming over, with Fuji-nee, mornings and nights.
It goes without saying that they're coming for breakfast and dinner.
The two have been living together for two months now, and they're practically joined at the hip.

page15.text:
When I pass near the shed wall...
I hear Sakura and Illya talking.

page16.text:
Illya is pretty blunt, so I thought she wouldn't get along with Sakura, but that doesn't seem to be the case.
They're like an odd couple... Illya is energetic, while Sakura is more laid-back. It seems they get along, in spite of their differences.
In fact, Sakura has regained her usual cheer thanks to Illya.

page17.text:
Ever since Sakura's older brother, Shinji, disappeared and was listed as missing, she'd stopped smiling.
She must have sensed that he had something to do with the mass coma incident at school.
Fretting over Shinji, Sakura shut herself away.

page18.text:
It was Illya who forced her to get over it, and Sakura is her normal, cheerful self whenever she's with Illya.
"Yep. Sakura's smiling again."
I'm truly happy about that.
Sakura's most herself when she's smiling that gentle smile of hers.

page19.text:
"Ugggh. Illya's so mean. I even offered her a little extra pocket money to wake me up, no matter what."
Fuji-nee is in tears as she shovels breakfast into her mouth.

page20.text: "I had no choice. If I waited for you to wake up, I would be late, and I worked enough to earn my pay. If you want me to work harder, then you should just raise my allowance rather than giving me a little extra sometimes."

page21.text:
"Hnnngh. I know you get money from Grandfather too. Why is this child such a miser?
Nobody will like you if you're so stingy at such a young age."

page22.text: "That's okay. As long as the person I like doesn't think like that, I don't care what anyone else thinks. Oh, by the way, Taiga, I want the money you borrowed the other day back. It was payday five days ago, right?"

page23.text:
"Eh? H-how do you know that!?"
"Raiga told me. I can give you the details of the conversation if you like."

page24.text:
Illya grins wryly.
Unlike her more friendly relationship with Sakura, Illya and Taiga are practically cats and dogs.
Illya gets really mean with Fuji-nee. Even her smile reminds me of a certain someone's smirk.

page25.text:
"You've got until tomorrow. If you can't pay me back, I'll take it out of your allowance, Taiga."
"What!? I-I can't believe Grandfather told you about that!"

page26.text:
"Yep. I'm with him all day. Raiga even said I'm cuter than you, Taiga."
"Whaaa...!? What have you done, Shirou!? This girl is the DEVIL! She's going to take over the whole Fujimura group!"

page27.text:
...
Uh, more importantly...
Why does a grown woman still get an allowance from her grandfather?

page28.text:
"See you later, Shirou. You're coming home early today, right? Then I'll wait here, so come home quick."
"Yep. I'll try. Take care of the house, Illya."

page29.text:
"Hmph. She might as well just live in this house, for all I care...dummy."
Fuji-nee sulks as she hides behind my back.
"Yeah, yeah. Buck up, Taiga. Don't give Shirou such a hard time."

page30.text:
Illya shrugs off Taiga's comment.
Looks like Fuji-nee isn't really in a position to push back against Illya.

page31.text:
"Well, I'm going ahead. Don't dawdle and wind up late for school, Shirou."
Fuji-nee lets out an engine roar and disappears like a speeding bullet.

page32.text:
She got her driver's license last month.
Since then, she's been late for school a lot less often, but now she has a new nickname: Rocket Tiger...er, Rocket Diver. She's the only one who doesn't know about it.

page33.text:
"Whew."
I stretch and take a deep breath.
Sakura already left for school.
She ate a pretty big bowl of rice this morning, so she must be pretty driven today.
Today is a big day for the kyudo club.
Now that she's the vice captain, Sakura must be really determined and enthusiastic today.

page34.text:
"All right. I should..."
Go to school too.
Today is April seventh.
Schools are starting the new school year, and the season has gone from the cold of winter to spring.

page35.text:
It's been two months.
I feel like a lot has changed since she left, but the changes all seem minor.

page36.text:
Winter is over and it's finally spring.
That's the only thing that's changed.
I might have grown and matured, but I'm not a different person or anything.
So, not that much has changed.
Shirou Emiya is still clumsily stumbling along in Kiritsugu's footsteps.

page37.text:
"Morning, Emiya. Fancy running into you in the morning."
"Hey there. Nice weather we have today, Tohsaka."
I wave in greeting.

page38.text:
"But is this really a coincidence? We run into each other almost every day.
Well sure, we never ran into each other that often before."
"Run into each other?"

page39.text:
Tohsaka narrows her eyes and glares at me, unhappy about how I phrased that.
I don't think getting angry so early in the morning is good for you.

page40.text: "Tohsaka, did you start leaving your house earlier? You always arrived later. You were never early or late to school."

page41.text:
"That's not true. It was just a coincidence that we never saw each other.
Did you know your house and mine are in opposite directions? So if we woke up at a normal time and walked down the hill at the same time, we would naturally meet up here."

page42.text:
"Huh.
That's news to me. Then I guess that's not so surprising—"
Wait a minute.
That's only possible if our daily schedules are the same.
For Tohsaka to reach this intersection at this hour, she'd have to wake up at six in the morning.
But that's...

page43.text:
"Tohsaka. You must be exhausted."
I just come right out and say it.

page44.text:
"What are you talking about? I'm not tired, and I'm not pushing myself either.
Why would you say that?"

page45.text:
"Well, because you're not a morning person.
If you go to school while you're half asleep, your Goody Two-shoes front might collapse. You'd be a goner if you fell asleep in class.
If someone woke you up, you'd go berserk and they'd see your true, terrifying face."
Like, "Who dares disturb my slumber" kind of terrifying.

page46.text:
"I-I would never do something like that! I would never make a mistake like that just because I woke up thirty minutes earlier!"
"Oh. So you did wake up earlier than usual."

page47.text:
"Grrr.
Oh, come on! It doesn't matter what time I get up! If you have time for trivial questions like that, then get to school!"
Tohsaka huffs and looks away.
She has a point, so I'm going to let this go and just resume our walk to school.

page48.text:
We walk up the hill.
The townscape below has bloomed into a springtime scene.
The breeze is pleasant, and the leaves of the cherry blossom tree planted near school dance on the wind from time to time.
It makes me smile.

page49.text:
"Hey. Are you mostly going to your job this week?
Not that it matters to me since it's your time and all, but you're not overworking yourself, are you?"
"Eh? No, I got a day off today.
I heard the kyudo club was holding a welcome party for the new members, so I figured I'd bring Illya to hang out."

page50.text: "Whoa. You've got guts. You don't even bat an eye at bringing Illya to school... You're something else."

page51.text:
"Huh? Is that bad? Illya seemed bored, so I thought this would be a good distraction."
"It's bad. Anyway, I might swing by too. Hard to be bored with Illya around, and most of all, it's too dangerous to just ignore this."

page52.text:
I'm grateful to hear her say that.
Tohsaka understands Illya much better than Sakura or I do.
It's not just that she periodically checks in on Illya's health. Tohsaka and Illya are both proper mages.
Illya still doesn't fully understand that she needs to hide the fact that she's a mage, so Tohsaka's been a great mentor for her in that regard.

page53.text:
...
And so, things are starting to settle in their respective places.
The new priest the Church dispatched has already repaired most of the damage from the Holy Grail War, and we've more or less gone back into our ordinary lives.
There are things lost that we can never get back, yes.
But the wounds are slowly healing, and I should be glad to know that some of the regrets I felt before are slowly fading.

page54.text:
"But that was unexpected."
Tohsaka mutters under her breath.
She looks down at the town, her tone serious.

page55.text:
"Huh? What was unexpected?"
"Well, I thought you'd be depressed.
I was worried it would take a while for you to recover from all this."

page56.text:
She's talking about...the girl who's not with me now.
It's been two months, and this is the first time we've brought up the golden-haired girl.

page57.text:
"Yeah. I didn't think I'd be able to recover from it either. I was going out of my mind just thinking what might happen afterward."
"But when it actually happened, you acted the same as always. You didn't seem depressed. You were even acting like nothing happened the next day."

page58.text: "That's when I started to get worried about whether you were really okay or not. I can't really explain it, but it felt like you were going to die in some freak accident the next day or something."

page59.text: "Freaking...what? How does me seeming fine end with me dead?"

page60.text:
"Things like that happen. A person just accidentally achieves their lifelong goal, then keels over and dies.
The moment they think they don't need to live anymore, a car runs them over, or they just fall down a set of stairs."

page61.text:
Huh.
That's...a little hard to get my head around.
I guess she's talking about dying after living a full life, or resting in peace, maybe.

page62.text:
"That's why I was worried that was going to happen. You know, there are times it's more normal to get spectacularly depressed."
"What? Would you have comforted me if I got all depressed?"

page63.text:
"Of course not. I would have kicked you in the butt and made you get over it in a day. I was just disappointed I didn't get the chance."
She turns away, displeased.
It's so funny, I can't help bursting into laughter.

page64.text:
"What? Was that funny?"
"No. Your tough-as-nails line was just so you, it was a relief."

page65.text:
We continue walking, enjoying the spring sunshine.
The hilly road is long, and it looks as if it continues into the endless blue sky.
Then, she brings something else up, surprisingly casually.

page66.text:
"So you don't have any regrets? You know, about Saber being gone."
Her eyes are on the sky as she speaks.

page67.text:
"Yeah...I don't have any regrets... Probably."
I'm not trying to put up a front. I even surprise myself with how at peace I sound.

page68.text:
Nothing was left unsaid, so I don't regret anything.
Everything went into the moment we said goodbye.
What I wanted to do...
What she dreamed...
Maybe we were both stubborn, and maybe I really should have grabbed her hand and made her dream come true.

page69.text:
But there was something we both felt was beautiful, and we both desperately tried to protect it until the very end.
I have no regrets.
As she properly ended her time...
I can't let myself be stuck in those memories forever.

page70.text:
"Huh. So you've already settled the matter for yourself.
So that's why you're not depressed, and you're just going to drown in your memories."

page71.text:
"Yeah. But I still dream about her. I'm going to remember her for the rest of my life.
One day, my memories of her will fade, and I'll forget her voice and her mannerisms.
But still...I'll never forget what happened, or that I loved her."

page72.text:
Tohsaka doesn't say a thing.
But for some reason, she looks elated. She's practically skipping now.

page73.text: "What's going on, Tohsaka? What's the rush? Did something happen?"

page74.text:
"Nothing. I just want to get to school quickly.
So come on! Hurry, Shirou! I'll leave you behind if you're too slow!"
She turns around and starts to run up the hill.

page75.text:
"What the hell? Why would she push herself when she's not a morning person?"
I grumble, then sling my bag onto my shoulder and run to catch up.
It's only seven-thirty in the morning.
It's too early for students who aren't involved in any club activities, but I guess there's nothing wrong with getting to school early.

page76.text: I run up the hilly road that seems to stretch into the sky, and I reach the school earlier than usual.

page77.text:
Today is the first day of the school year.
If I want to celebrate, I need to shake off old memories.
Remnants of my memory will never go away.
But I still need to go on, even if the emptiness in my heart makes me cry...

page78.text:
The blue sky is off in the distance.
It feels so close...
...but even if I reached out, I could never grasp it.

page79.text:
I've looked to the stars before.
There are unreachable stars and unfulfilled wishes.
Nothing of ours remains behind.
So, someday, my memories of her, even the image of her face will disappear.
...
And yet...
Even if I can't ever reach her, something will remain in our hearts.

page80.text:
There may be nothing physical left, but we both shared time together and looked up at the same things.
If I can remember that...I can believe that we're still together, even across such a great distance.
Some things are bound to disappear, but others never will.

page81.text:
So I'm going to keep running.
If I push far enough, I might one day reach what I was aiming for.

page82.text:
The new beginnings of spring...after the end of a harsh winter.
I head up the hill under the same blue sky she looked up and saw.

page83.text:
The battle is over.
This is her final battlefield...the battle that split her country in half, and ended with the king's victory.

page84.text:
"Haaah...ha...haaa...ha!"
The knight runs to her.
The battle is over. The bloodred sunset has faded, and now the darkness of night covers the battlefield.
The hill is littered with corpses and curses. All that resentment tries to drag the survivors down with it.

page85.text:
Through it all, the knight runs, breathless.
He grips his horse's reins as the wounded white steed does its best to keep up.
The knight and the white horse are the only survivors.
Draped over the horse's back is the wounded king.

page86.text:
"Your Majesty! King Arthur...this way!"
The knight must be wounded himself, but he runs with all his might.
The king he serves is on the verge of death.
Even after defeating the rival king in single combat, his king sustained a fatal wound.
The knight knows there is no hope here.
His king will die soon.

page87.text:
"Please stay with me! If we manage to reach that forest, you shall...!"
He calls desperately to his king.
Or perhaps the knight truly believes...
...that his king is immortal.
So long as they have the guidance of the sacred sword, the king will never perish.

page88.text:
"Ha...haaa...ha...ha...ha!"
With labored breathing, the knight crosses the mountain of corpses and heads to a forest that has not yet been stained in blood.
He knows of his king's immortality.
So he believes that if he can only escape this cursed battlefield and lead the king somewhere pure, the king's wounds will be healed.

page89.text:
Or rather...he hopes.
Unlike the other knights, he always believed in his king.
The king had always been isolated at court, shunned by the knights, and feared by the people.
But the knight was proud of the young king, who never revealed any personal feelings, no matter the situation, and always remained idealistic.

page90.text:
The knight did not serve his country.
And that is why he entrusted his sword to his king, strove to aid his king, and rose to the position of the king's personal guard despite his young age.
The king whose true face can never be seen.
The boy tried to be fair and selfless, and did not allow his personal feelings to interfere with his duties.
Rather, he hoped that if he could someday get close enough, he could see his king's real face.

page91.text:
That is his greatest desire.
He wants so much to see his king's true face...not the stern countenance the king bore on the battlefield, but his king's true face...a smiling, laughing, human face.
That moment would surely come in court, when the king is relieved of all duty.
Even the most perfect king cannot be on edge all the time.

page92.text:
The knight was proved wrong, though.
What he learned defied his expectations.
He reached the rank of imperial guard and stood guard at the king's side.
He guarded the king more closely than any knight, and always observed the king's behavior.
But the moment he wished for never came.
His king never smiled.

page93.text:
"Ha...haaa...ha...ha...ha!"
Why does that make him so angry?
The king should radiate glory, having achieved such success.
But never once did the king seem at ease, even for a moment.
He couldn't stand it.
He wanted to believe this shouldn't happen.
And so he wished for his king to be rewarded with light.

page94.text:
That has yet to be accomplished.
The king still remains solitary.
And so the knight refuses to accept his king's death.
It cannot end here.
If it does, this great king will never be rewarded.

page95.text:
"Your Majesty, please stay here. I will summon reinforcements right away."
Once they reach the forest, the knight leans his king's body against a large tree.
It is a race against time.
Even riding hard on horseback, it will take half a day to bring back the troops they left at the harbor.
Any who see the king now would know that the king will not last until dawn.

page96.text:
"Please, hold on until then. I promise I will bring our troops back here."
The knight bows to his half-conscious king, and returns to his white steed.
"...Bedivere."
Before he can leave...
...the king he thought unconscious calls out to him.

page97.text:
"Your Majesty!? Have you woken up!?"
"Yes... I was having a dream."
The king's voice is faint.
But there is warmth in it.

page98.text:
"A dream...sire?"
The knight's voice is imploring.
The king's life is balanced on the tip of a blade. The darkness will surely take his king if the knight does not respond.
"Yes. I have not had many dreams, so it was valuable experience."
"That is wonderful. Please, have a pleasant rest. I will call for reinforcements while you do."

page99.text:
"..."
A faint gasp.
The knight's words must have been unexpected.

page100.text:
"Your...Majesty? Have I said something to offend...?"
"No, you only surprised me. Can you still dream after you've woken? Are you saying I will return to that same dream after I close my eyes?"
Now it's the knight's turn to be surprised.
For a moment, he is at a loss for words. At length, he responds, though he knows there is no truth to what he says.

page101.text:
"Yes. If you truly desire it, you will indeed return to the same dream. I have experienced it myself."
It's not possible.
A dream is a fleeting thing...not something to return to.
Even so, the knight lies to his king.
It is the first and last time he will do such a thing.

page102.text:
"I see. You are quite knowledgeable, Bedivere."
The king's soft voice is admirable.
The king's head remains tilted down, not looking up at the knight.
The king breathes so softly that it can be barely audible.
"Bedivere. Take my sword."
The knight receives his king's final order.

page103.text:
"Listen. Pass through the forest and travel over that bloody hill. Beyond that, you will find a lake. Throw my sword into it."
"What!? Your Majesty...that would mean...!"
The knight knows what that means.
The sword in the lake.
To relinquish the sword that had protected the king and served as proof of kingship...would mean the end of his king.

page104.text:
"Go. Once you have fulfilled my order, return here and tell me what you saw."
The king does not take back orders.
The knight takes the sacred sword and goes over the hill...his indecision weighing heavily on him.

page105.text:
And so...
Three times, the knight hesitates to follow his king's command.
The lake looms in front of him.
But he cannot throw the sword away.
Doing so means his king will disappear.
The knight's unwillingness to part with his king stays his hand, and so he returns to his king.

page106.text:
Once again, the king orders him to throw the sword into the lake.
When the knight lies and claims he's thrown the sword into the lake as ordered, his king simply replies, "Do as I have commanded you."
To defy the king's order is a great sin for a knight.
But he has already done so twice.
Each time he stands before the lake, he hesitates at the thought of losing his king.

page107.text:
No more.
When the knight realizes he cannot alter his king's decision, on his third visit, he hurls the sword into the lake.
The sacred sword returns to the lake.
A white hand emerges from the water and catches the blade, and the sacred sword vanishes from the world.

page108.text:
...
And the knight finally accepts it.
The end of his king.
The responsibilities that had so long burdened the knight finally come to an end.

page109.text:
By the third time he crosses the hill, the first rays of morning light touch the forest.
The ruins of the battlefield now distant.
There is no trace of the bloody battle. Only a thin haze covers the hill.

page110.text:
"I've thrown the sword into the lake. It is back in the hands of the Lady of the Lake."
At the knight's words, the king's eyes open.
"I see. Then you must stand proud. You have obeyed your king's command."

page111.text:
The knight gives a silent nod to that voice, knowing the speaker is on the brink of death.
It's all over.
Turmoil will continue to grip the nation. The wars will not end. The day of ruin will come soon.
But the king's battle is over.
Because he...or rather, she fulfilled her role till the very end.

page112.text:
The light fades.
With everything done, the last of the strength that kept her going is spent.
"I must apologize, Bedivere.
This sleep will...be a...long one..."
She closes her eyes...
Slowly...as if going to sleep...

page113.text:
The morning light spills through the treetops.
As the king drifts to her eternal rest, a hush falls over the forest.

page114.text:
...
The knight continues his vigil over the fallen king.
The king he wished for.
The solitary king, attended by only a single knight.
And he finally sees the look he hoped for on his king's face:
A peaceful sleep.
In her last moments, the king finally finds the peace that had so long eluded her.

page115.text:
The knight is overjoyed.
The knight thanks whoever gave his king such comfort, and watches the king with a sense of pride.

page116.text:
The heavens are distant, and the clear sky is blue.
The battle is truly over.
